problems.what: every Pose number lerps linearly and only the disc and triangle angles take the short way, so bars and rules glide their raw angles: across the mirror line (bar 6 to 7 and the seam) the long vertical bar swings 180 degrees through horizontal and the diagonal rule 90, sweeping across the whole frame in six frames; the triangle spins 180 degrees in B to C (00:03.8); and outBack(1.3) puts its overshoot on those angles, so the landing frames (57-59 of each bar) show bars, rules and the triangle tilted 10-20 degrees: the arrival wobbles instead of landing
problems.fix: glide each angle to its nearest symmetric equivalent (bars and rules mod 180, triangle mod 120, square mod 90, disc and arc start the short way round) and ease angles with outCubic (no overshoot); only positions and sizes keep the outBack weight

problems.what: the title lerps position, size and angle from the margin into the composition, so for three frames 'three shapes' is set diagonally across the red square, the bars and the circle; leaving bars 1 and 7 it does the same in reverse
problems.fix: the title never glides: it lands large on the downbeats of bars 1 and 7 (with the hits at 0 and 360) and snaps back to the margin on beat 4 of those bars, both on the beat grid

problems.what: the ground band that shows the score is too small to read at phone size: the hats flick 22 px, the dots are 16 px across, so at 360 px wide the hats are a 7 px twitch (3-4 px in landscape) and the arpeggio a row of specks; the study's premise, shapes playing the score, is illegible in the one place it is literal, and about 70 px of paper under it is unused
problems.fix: move the hats down into the unused margin, make them jump about 40 px and scale bar width and dot radius with the band's step (larger in landscape), with a bigger bump on the current red dot

problems.what: the beat-1 bass note is absorbed into the recomposition, so the triangle visibly steps only once a bar (beat 3), not on beats 1 and 3 as the brief maps it
problems.fix: not fixed this round; would need the triangle to finish its glide half a step early and step on the downbeat
